extracted.intended_audience: members of Parliament and the informed public
extracted.subtask_description: A parliamentary/legislative speech critiquing the legitimacy, contracting, and enforcement of debt claims and assignments involving the East India Company and the Nabob of Arcot (late 18th-century context). Focuses on legality, authority, fraud, and public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent required for debt (no free loans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every debt, for which an equivalent of some kind or other is not given, is, on the face of it, a fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a claimed debt corresponds to a real transfer of property/value (goods, services, or lawful payment). The speech demands evidence of what equivalent the creditors gave — no trade, sciences, arts, or institutions were exported that could justify the millions claimed. If no equivalent exists, treat claims as fraudulent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt must be contracted with the Company's knowledge and approbation
rubrics_metrics.description: A legitimate loan should have been contracted with the knowledge and approbation of the Court of Directors; debts concealed from the Company are suspicious or invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check company records and correspondence: the Directors said the dealings were 'concealed from us' and that they received intelligence only years later. Lack of prior notification or approval by the appropriate authority is evidence against the claim's legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government should not enforce claims founded on a defiance of authority
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary that the authority of government should interpose in favor of claims whose very foundation was a defiance of that authority, and whose object is its subversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim arises from actions intended to overthrow or evade lawful authority, public institutions should not be used to support enforcement; such matters ought to be left to the private parties involved rather than made public liabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: No concealment by Company's servants; concealment = breach of duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Concealing transactions from the Court of Directors constitutes a high breach of duty and is indicative of corrupt conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether local officials or servants intentionally hid assignments or loans. The Directors' language ('to your great reproach, it has been concealed from us') is offered as a standard: concealment is prima facie misconduct warranting punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments of territorial revenues require proper authorization; private assignments are breach of trust
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignment of districts' revenues or other territorial revenues to private creditors by Company servants (without authorization) is a manifest violation of trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine deeds/assignments (example: assignment of fifteen districts yielding eight lacs of pagodas) and whether trustees/agents acted as creditors and agents simultaneously. Unauthorised territorial assignments that divert public revenue to private creditors indicate illegitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usury and compounding of interest indicate fraud/abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Very high rates of interest (30–36% reduced later to 20% then labelled as '10%') and the practice of adding arrears to principal (forming new capital with interest-on-interest) signal fraudulent or usurious practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize the effective rate over time and the accounting of arrears: if arrears were capitalized repeatedly to create inflated claims, treat the debt as usurious and suspect. The reduction to a 'moderate' rate on paper may be the result of prior compounding, not fair lending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Presidency approval does not substitute for Company sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval by a local Presidency (e.g., Madras Presidency) does not equal sanction by the Court of Directors; the latter's disavowal matters for legitimacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish approvals: verify whether the central authority (Court of Directors) formally approved the transaction. The Presidency acting as creditor or trustee for debts is not sufficient authority if the Directors condemn the acts as a breach of trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative protections against abuse must be preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative clauses intended to prevent abuse (e.g., forbidding British subjects from receiving assignments on territorial revenue) should not be expunged; removing them opens a 'broad highway' for usury and oppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating policy or bills, check for retention of anti-abuse provisions. The speaker criticizes the expunging of an express clause in Mr. Fox's bill that forbade assignments — removal of such safeguards is culpable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creditors exercising political influence over Company/government indicates corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: When private creditors qualify votes, become masters of the Court of Proprietors, or create cabals to overturn directors, it demonstrates corrupt acquisition of influence to secure their claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether creditors used debt to buy political power or influence (e.g., making themselves masters of the Court of Proprietors). Such influence used to secure public enforcement of private claims is indicia of corruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims should not be satisfied out of public revenues that harm populace or military pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Satisfying private claims out of the public revenues (e.g., revenues of the Carnatic), or diverting funds that feed armies and people, is unjust and equivalent to extortion/usury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace the source of any funds proposed for settlement: if payment would come from taxes, military pay, or public sustenance, the claim should be treated with great skepticism and likely resisted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs of claims must be timely, disclosed, and available to rightful authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs produced long after publication of charges (e.g., proofs only presented to a local court years later) are suspect; claimants had a duty to give satisfaction to the Company earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require chronological transparency about when evidence was offered and to whom. Late, belated, or selectively revealed proofs do not vindicate longstanding published accusations and should be scrutinized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loans must be real advances of money, not paper swaps or circular bookkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Transactions in which bankers post notes as ready money without advancing cash, or where bonds/payments are effectively paid by assignment of the debtor's own revenues, are fraudulent soucaring practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether actual cash changed hands or whether 'notes' and assignments merely reshuffled claims. The described practice (banker putting notes in the cash-book while advancing no cash, charging the Nabob heavy monthly interest) is an anti-pattern for legitimate lending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public office holders must not personally profit from their positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Servants of the Company who enrich themselves (buy lands, seats in Parliament, houses) using their offices are betraying public trust; private aggrandizement at public expense is condemned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate conflicts of interest and post-service enrichment: patterns of sudden wealth among office holders, especially without visible means, are evidence of malpractice and should trigger inquiry and sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts made under usurped or illegitimate authority are invalid
rubrics_metrics.description: Transactions contracted by an usurped Council (e.g., the 1777 loan by a Council that overthrew lawful government) represent illegitimate authority and the debts contracted thereby are not rightful claims on the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the provenance of authority: if a governing body that made the contract did so after subverting lawful government, its acts (including loans and assignments) may be voidable and subject to prosecution.
